items.title: Renew Chandler business registration
items.authority: City of Chandler Tax and License Division
items.description: Businesses operating from a physical Chandler location need a city business registration for each location and entity, renewed annually, in addition to the state TPT license.

items.title: Hold a Town of Gilbert business license
items.authority: Town of Gilbert Tax Compliance Division
items.description: Businesses with a physical location in Gilbert need a Town business license; this is separate from the state-administered transaction privilege tax license.

items.title: Renew Glendale business license
items.authority: City of Glendale Licensing and Sales Tax
items.description: Any business with a permanent physical location in Glendale needs a city business license, renewed every year; a late penalty can apply when an application or renewal is more than 30 days late. TPT is licensed separately through the state.

items.title: Hold a Mesa general business license
items.description: Most businesses operating in Mesa need a general business license (since January 3, 2022). Businesses with taxable activity also need a valid Arizona TPT license with the Mesa location added.

items.title: Hold a Peoria business license
items.authority: City of Peoria Sales Tax and Business License
items.description: The city requires a business license for anyone conducting business in Peoria, including home-based businesses; reviews can take up to 30 days and the state TPT license is separate.

items.title: Obtain City of Phoenix transaction privilege (sales) tax license
items.authority: City of Phoenix Finance Department, Tax Compliance and Education
items.description: Businesses making taxable sales within Phoenix hold a city privilege tax license and report city TPT in addition to the state TPT; retail tax is based on the seller's location.

note: Only the state-administered TPT license was confirmed from the city's pages; a separate city business registration was not.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Scottsdale
items.description: Review the cited local licensing source before operating; requirements may be activity-specific and can differ by business type or location.

items.title: Hold a City of Surprise business license
items.description: Businesses operating in Surprise need a city business license, reviewed in up to 20 calendar days with payment requested after review; the state TPT license is separate.

items.title: Renew Tempe general business license
items.authority: City of Tempe Financial Services, Sales Tax and Licensing
items.description: The general business license (effective August 1, 2025) applies to businesses with a permanent Tempe location, including those with no TPT license; the first renewal is due before January 1, 2027 and annually after that. Regulatory licenses are separate.
items.deadline: Before January 1 each year (first renewal before January 1, 2027)

items.title: Renew Tucson business license
items.authority: City of Tucson Business Services Department
items.description: Businesses in Tucson hold a city business license in addition to the state transaction privilege tax license, renewed annually.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Buckeye
items.description: Buckeye publishes city business-license fees by business type; common mercantile, professional, restaurant, and mobile-food licenses have a $25 application fee and $50 annual fee, with a $25 late fee.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Goodyear
items.description: Goodyear requires every person conducting business within the city, whether or not they have a fixed location, to obtain a city business license; businesses should apply through the city's Business License Request Form.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Yuma
items.description: Yuma requires businesses to obtain the applicable city business license; the city publishes the complete fee schedule and license code through its Business License and Sales Tax Office, with tax periods due in advance under city code.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Avondale
items.description: Avondale business licenses are annual; the city's fee schedule lists a $40 annual license fee, a $25 processing fee, and renewal late fees, with application-period fees varying by quarter.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Queen Creek
items.description: Queen Creek requires all businesses located or operating in town to obtain a license before beginning; a new license costs $60, expires 12 months after issue, and renewal is annual with a $40 in-town renewal fee.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Maricopa
items.description: Maricopa generally does not issue business licenses; regulated businesses must obtain a city regulated-business license after zoning approval, with an annual initial or renewal fee of $50.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Flagstaff
items.description: Flagstaff requires a Transaction Privilege (sales) Tax License for taxable business activity; the city lists a $20 license fee and $20 annual renewal fee, filed through the Arizona Department of Revenue process.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Casa Grande
items.description: Casa Grande requires a city business tax receipt after applicable approvals; home-based businesses must obtain a Home Occupation Permit, which carries a $31.50 application fee, before obtaining the city business tax receipt.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Marana
items.description: Marana requires businesses conducting business in town to obtain a license; the standard license costs $60 new, $40 annually to renew, and becomes subject to a $10 late fee 15 days after expiration.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Lake Havasu City
items.authority: Lake Havasu City local licensing authority
items.description: Lake Havasu City requires a business license before operating; licenses run for one year from approval and renew annually, with city license fees of $5, $25, or $50 depending on the class.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Prescott Valley
items.description: Prescott Valley requires applicable business registration and license fees under its municipal code; the town's published fee analysis lists a $45 business-license fee and $45 annual renewal fee, subject to late-renewal penalties.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Prescott
items.description: Prescott businesses engaged in taxable activity must obtain an Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax license and file the applicable city tax returns; the city lists a $5 privilege-tax license application fee and $5 annual renewal fee.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Oro Valley
items.description: Oro Valley requires a general business or home-occupation license; the annual fee is $80, prorated by month, and the town reports a typical processing time of 3–5 business days.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Apache Junction
items.description: Apache Junction requires approval and payment before a business may operate; the city business-license fee is $50, with separate privilege-tax or operating-license requirements possible by business type.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Sierra Vista
items.description: Sierra Vista requires businesses to use the city's business-license process before operating; separate licenses may apply by activity, and the city publishes the current application and renewal instructions through its Business Licenses office.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in Bullhead City
items.description: Bullhead City requires a business license to operate; the typical general license costs $60 annually plus a one-time $60 application fee, with amounts varying by license type.

items.title: Review applicable local licenses and permits in San Luis
items.description: San Luis requires a business-license application to be filed and approved before lawful operation; the Arizona TPT license fee for San Luis is $2, and the city reviews applications through multiple departments.
